approach: Add `check_measure_then_fix(reading)` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and wire it as one `step!` line after `check_criteria_evidence`. This revision drops the recorded-timings exemption and the bare-word signals. The check now reads only the reading's criteria and deliverables, and it refuses when two things hold. (1) Run signal: a non-meta criterion sentence directs a new full timed workspace test run. That means a directive verb (run, time, measure, record, collect, capture, rerun) plus a full-run phrase plus a timing word. A sentence that mentions the reading, request, refusal or a rule describes the rule and does not count. (2) Fix signal: either a deliverable that is Rust code or a test (`.rs` under `crates/` or `xtask/`), or a non-meta criterion with a full-form fix word and a dependency phrase. A fix-only reading is accepted because it has no run signal, so it needs no exemption. The error says to split into a measurement stage and a fix stage and to plan the measurement stage only. Also add unit tests, `measure-then-fix` corpus cases, a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Refuse in the reading gate (a new `step!` in `refusing_check`), not in the orchestrator or the producer brief.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading is accepted. The gate lets two dependent steps (a long run of unknown outcome and a fix chosen from it) into one producer run with one deadline and budget. The corpus mechanism test forces a refusing case for each `step!`.

rejected.option: Chain or split jobs automatically in the orchestrator
rejected.why: Out of scope, and a much larger design.

rejected.option: Raise the producer deadline or budget
rejected.why: Out of scope, and a run of unknown outcome has no safe bound.

rejected.option: Advice in the producer brief only
rejected.why: Prose is not enforcement, and the producer is past the point where the deadline fails.

decisions.choice: Drop the recorded-timings exemption entirely (finding 1). A fix-only reading passes because it has no run signal, not because it names a file or says 'recorded'.
decisions.reason: A name-based exemption lets a joined reading that names xtask/shard-timings.txt through. `has_phrase` also treats '-' as a boundary, so 'already-recorded timings' would exempt anything. The run signal is defined by what a criterion directs. 'recorded' is not the directive verb 'record', and `has_phrase` is whole-word, so 'recorded timings from the full timed run' is not a run signal.

rejected.why: Defeats the check for the most likely joined wording.

rejected.option: Exempt only when no criterion directs a run
rejected.why: That is what the run signal already does, so a separate exemption is redundant.

decisions.choice: Scan criteria and deliverables only, not title and summary. A run-signal sentence must have a directive verb and no meta word (reading, readings, request, refus*, rule). Sentences split at '. ', ';' and newlines (finding 2).
decisions.reason: A reading about this check describes the shape, for example criterion 1 of this job: 'a reading whose request joins a full timed workspace test run with a fix'. It has no directive, and 'reading' and 'request' are meta words. A test built from this job's six criteria verbatim must be accepted. A test plus a corpus case pin it, so widening the phrase lists later cannot silently refuse rule-editing readings.

rejected.option: Match the bare phrases anywhere in title, summary and criteria
rejected.why: Refuses readings that document or edit the rule, including this job's own reading.

decisions.choice: Take the fix signal from structure first (a `.rs` code or test deliverable), with a second path of a full-form fix word plus a dependency phrase in a non-meta criterion (findings 3 and 4). The dependency phrase is no longer required in the structural path.
decisions.reason: 'Time the full run; then speed up the slowest binary' has no dependency phrase but does list code deliverables, so it is still refused. A joined reading that lists only a CHANGELOG deliverable (the fix is not known before the run) is caught by the word path. Fix words are listed in full form, because `has_phrase` matches whole words: fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, speed up, speeds up, speed-up, optimise, optimize, optimised, optimized, optimisation, optimization, shorten, shortens. A unit variant covers each form.

rejected.option: Require all of run phrase, fix word and dependency phrase

rejected.why: Needs a non-whole-word matcher beside `has_phrase`; full forms are simpler and tested.

decisions.choice: Add a seventh `READING_RULES` line for `check_measure_then_fix` in briefs.rs, and update the brief tests (length 7, check-name list, section-size bound).
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks that the reader brief name the check. The existing test pairs each check name with its own line of at most 220 bytes.

rejected.option: Fold it into an existing rule line
rejected.why: The test pairs each check name with its own line.

decisions.choice: Cover the rule with one new corpus form tag `measure-then-fix` and six cases, plus unit tests.
decisions.reason: `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` fails for a listed form with no case. The corpus runs the whole gate on request-shaped input. Unit tests cover the variants.

rejected.why: They would not show gate order or the request-bullet path.

steps: Read reading.rs around `refusing_check` and `check_criteria_evidence` (lines 3047-3311). Add `pub fn check_measure_then_fix(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` after `check_criteria_evidence`. Return Ok if `capability` is None or `question` is Some. For each criterion, normalise as `producer_evidence_phrase` does (lowercase, curly apostrophes made straight, whitespace collapsed). Split it into sentences at '. ', ';' and newline. A mid-token dot such as `shard-timings.txt` is not a split point. Match with `has_phrase`.

Run signal: a sentence with (a) a directive verb among run, time, measure, record, collect, capture, rerun; (b) a full-run phrase among 'full workspace test', 'whole workspace test', 'full test suite', 'full timed', 'timed workspace test', 'timed test run'; (c) a timing word among timed, timing, timings; and (d) none of the meta words reading, readings, request, refuse, refused, refuses, refusal, rule. There is no exemption for recorded timings or file names.

Fix signal, either of: (a) a deliverable whose path ends `.rs` and starts `crates/` or `xtask/`; (b) a non-meta criterion with a full-form fix word (fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, speed up, speeds up, speed-up, optimise, optimize, optimised, optimized, optimisation, optimization, shorten, shortens) and a dependency phrase (chosen from, based on the timings, based on the result, from its result, from the result, from the timings, from the measurements, from the slowest, depends on the result). Refuse when a run signal and a fix signal both hold. Error text: the reading joins a full timed workspace test run with a fix chosen from its result in one producer run with one deadline and budget; split it into a measurement stage (its only deliverable is the timings entry, written as soon as the run finishes) and a fix stage that cites the recorded timings; plan the measurement stage only.

risks.risk: False refusals: an ordinary reading that directs a full timed run and lists code deliverables is refused.
risks.mitigation: The run signal needs a directive verb, a full-run phrase and a timing word in one non-meta sentence. A bare 'cargo test --workspace' is not a run signal. The corpus cases `measurement-only-reading`, `fix-only-reading-cites-recorded-timings` and `measure-then-fix-rule-reading-itself` pin the accepted side.

risks.risk: The meta-word list lets a joined sentence slip through if it contains 'request' or 'reading', for example 'run the full timed workspace test and record the request latency'.
risks.mitigation: Meta words are matched as whole words and only exclude the run sentence. The fix signal is checked separately. A unit test covers a joined criterion with a neutral sentence next to a meta sentence, and the list stays short (reading, readings, request, refus*, rule).

risks.risk: The reader retries once and cannot produce an accepted reading.
risks.mitigation: The error says to narrow the reading to the measurement stage. A reading with no code deliverable and no fix criterion passes (unit test (f) and the corpus case `measurement-only-reading`).

risks.risk: An earlier check refuses a new corpus case first.
risks.mitigation: Put the `step!` after `check_criteria_evidence`. Use the docs class with Content criteria, keep the case text free of producer-report wording, and give code-deliverable cases only a path that is in `repo_files()`.

risks.risk: The reader brief's rules section exceeds the existing `< 2400` size test with a seventh line.
risks.mitigation: Raise the bound to 2700, keep the line at most 220 bytes, and run `cargo test -p athena-context`. Edit only `READING_RULES`, which sits outside the budgeted prompt sets, so `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` is unaffected.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in `mod tests` of reading.rs call `check_measure_then_fix` and `refusing_check` on real `Reading` values. Refused: (a) a joined reading, with 'measurement stage' and 'fix stage' in the error. (b) Case, line-break and wording variants. (c) A reading that names xtask/shard-timings.txt and is still joined (finding 1). (d) A paraphrase ('time the full workspace test run; then speed up the slowest binary') with a `.rs` deliverable (finding 4). (e) One variant per fix word form: fixes, fixed, fixing, optimise, optimize, optimization, speeds up (finding 3). Accepted: (f) measurement-only. (g) Fix-only, citing recorded timings, with a code deliverable and no run. (h) This job's own title, summary and six criteria verbatim, with `.rs` deliverables (finding 2). (i) A decline and a question. (j) `refusing_check` names `check_measure_then_fix` for a joined reading that passes the earlier checks.

open_questions: The request texts of jobs 20261031-043143-vbee and 20261102-154842-4vkh are not in the snapshot (records are absent; the brief truncates the cause). The corpus cases are rebuilt from the brief's description, so the exact criterion wording the producer must match is unverified.

The check reads the reading, not the raw request, so a reader that narrows a joined request to the measurement stage passes. A reading that paraphrases the run away from a directive verb plus a full-run phrase plus a timing word passes too. Widening the lists is a cheap follow-up.

A reading that directs a full timed run and also changes `.rs` files for an unrelated reason, such as adding a timing harness, is refused. The error tells the reader to plan the run stage only. The 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' figure is an estimate, not measured.

Input forms with no new case: star bullets and `1.`, `1)` and `(a)` parts only change how criteria are extracted before the check runs. The existing cases `star-bullets`, `numbered-dot-parts`, `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today` and `lettered-paren-parts-not-read-today` cover them. The case ids in this plan are ones I read in the base file or ones step 4 adds; I did not run the corpus.
